exampleAnswers.title: Identifying Elements of a Multiple Linear Regression

question.text:
$x_1$ $-2$ $-1$ $0$ $1$ $2$
$x_2$ $6$ $11$ $8$ $20$ $24$
$y$ $0$ $-1$ $4$ $9$ $16$

The vector of coefficients of the plane $y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2$ that best fits the data above can be found using multi linear regression as

\[ \begin{bmatrix} \beta_0 \\ \beta_1 \\ \beta_2 \end{bmatrix} = (X^T \! X)^{-1} X^T \mathbf{y}, \]

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $\mathbf{y}$ in this context?
question.explanation:
$x_1$ $\color{blue}-2$ $\color{blue}-1$ $\color{blue}0$ $\color{blue}1$ $\color{blue}2$
$x_2$ $\color{purple}6$ $\color{purple}11$ $\color{purple}8$ $\color{purple}20$ $\color{purple}24$
$y$ $\color{red}0$ $\color{red}-1$ $\color{red}4$ $\color{red}9$ $\color{red}16$

The coefficients of the plane

\[ y=\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2 \]

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system

\begin{align*} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & \color{blue}-2 & \color{purple}6 \\ 1 & \color{blue}-1& \color{purple}11 \\ 1 & \color{blue}0& \color{purple}8\\ 1 & \color{blue}1 & \color{purple}20 \\ 1 & \color{blue}2 & \color{purple}24 \end{bmatrix} }^{X} \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \beta_0 \\ \beta_1 \\ \beta_2 \\ \beta_3 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \boldsymbol{\beta}} &= \overbrace{ \begin{bmatrix} \color{red}0 \\ \color{red}-1 \\ \color{red}4 \\ \color{red}9 \\ \color{red}16 \end{bmatrix} }^{ \mathbf{y}}, \end{align*}

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.
